clue.text: Sky feature, series inspiring a popular book

indicators.note: to inspire is literally to breathe in, so the series takes the other pieces into itself

parts.note: a row is a series of things in a line
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: Someone describes a TV or book series whose bestselling tie-in book was prompted by something seen in the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: An arc of colours seen after rain is a classic example of something that appears overhead.

clue.text: No, not something a showjumper wants?

definitions.meaning: a no is a turning-down of a request
in show jumping a horse balking at a fence is penalised

explanation.surface: An answer of 'no' is the last thing a rider at a horse show hopes for.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying no is a rejection; a horse balking at a jump commits a fault of this name.

clue.text: Middle son keeps away from wrongdoer

indicators.note: the son stays out of the word, so his letter is removed from it

parts.note: a sinner is a wrongdoer

explanation.surface: A middle child, a son, avoids a criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Middle' sounds like a description of the son but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something central, near the centre or core, is interior, the opposite of outer.

clue.text: Reportedly canal boat pilot is making spicy snack

indicators.note: reportedly means as said or heard, so we need a word that sounds like the pilot

parts.note: a bargee is someone who steers a barge on a canal

explanation.surface: A narrowboat skipper is cooking a hot snack in the galley.
explanation.definitionFit: An Indian fritter of vegetables in spiced gram-flour batter, often onion, served as a starter.

clue.text: One complaining of coach ultimately punching footballer

indicators.note: a punch lands in the footballer, so that letter goes inside the word

parts.note: a winger is a footballer who plays on the wing

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so take the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A player complains that his coach in the end hit a footballer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who moans and grumbles constantly, in British slang, is a person given to complaints.

clue.text: Husband Bill feeds pigs and dogs

indicators.note: what feeds the pigs goes into their mouths, so the first pieces go inside the word for pigs

parts.note: sows are female pigs
an ad, or advertisement, is a bill posted up

explanation.surface: A husband sees to feeding the farm animals: the pigs and the dogs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dogs' looks like animals alongside the pigs but is a verb: to follow someone closely.
explanation.definitionFit: To dog someone is to follow them persistently, just as a tail or detective trails a suspect.

clue.text: Is fairly discontented after school test answer

indicators.note: after says the following pieces come behind the school test

parts.note: SAT is a standardised school test

indicators.note: dis-contented means emptied of contents, leaving only the outer letters

explanation.surface: A student is somewhat unhappy after an exam answer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discontented' looks like unhappiness but means emptied, keeping F and Y. 'answer' is the verb, as in answering a need.
explanation.definitionFit: To answer a need or requirement is to meet or fulfil it, as a solution meets a demand.

clue.text: Marian periodically raised fuss about sick creature

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means the letters are read upward, backwards
periodically means at regular intervals, so take every other letter of the name
the fuss goes about the sick piece, holding it inside

parts.note: ado means fuss
ill means sick

explanation.surface: Marian keeps making a fuss over an unwell animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'periodically' takes Marian's odd letters, which 'raised' turns upward in this down clue; 'sick' is a piece, not the creature's state.
explanation.definitionFit: An armoured South American mammal is an animal, so it counts as a living creature.

clue.text: Bad international spies, extremely lawless government agents, say

parts.note: off means bad, as with food gone sour
the CIA is the American spy agency

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes of the word, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Rogue international spies, utterly lawless, posing as agents of the state.
explanation.definitionFit: Functionaries holding public office act for the state, so government agents are examples of such people.

clue.text: Mistake over blocking comedy sketch displaying root vegetable

indicators.note: a thing blocking a gap fills it, so it goes inside the sketch

parts.note: a skit is a short comic sketch

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the word for mistake is read backwards

parts.note: to err is to make a mistake

explanation.surface: A blunder in a comedy sketch shows off a vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: An old European plant grown for its sweet edible roots, a member of the carrot family.

clue.text: Duke describes worker as a Walter Mitty character

indicators.note: in crosswords to describe can mean to draw around, so the fist encircles the other pieces

parts.note: dukes is slang for fists, from the boxing phrase 'put up your dukes'
a worker ant is the stock crossword worker

explanation.surface: A duke characterises one of his labourers as a daydreamer.
explanation.walkthrough: Walter Mitty is the hero of a James Thurber story who lives in heroic daydreams.
explanation.definitionFit: A Walter Mitty figure lives in fantasies of heroism, the very picture of a daydreamer who invents a grander life.

clue.text: Civilian militia, unfit for training, it's initially …

definitions.note: used here as in 'civilian dress', the noun the answer names

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each of the preceding five words

explanation.surface: A civilian militia is judged unfit, so they go off for training, and the sentence runs on into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this clue to the next one; it is surface only.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain clothes worn by someone normally in uniform are called by this term, so it stands for civilian dress.

clue.text: … helping what current soldiers are doing?

definitions.meaning: a helping is a portion of food at a meal
soldiers still in the forces are said to be in active service

explanation.surface: The sentence from the previous clue continues: the training is a help, and it is what soldiers on duty are up to.
explanation.definitionFit: A plateful handed out at dinner is a portion; soldiers presently enlisted are on active duty in the army.

clue.text: I hurried around in pursuit of small cocktail

indicators.note: pursuing means coming behind, so these pieces follow the small one
turned around means the word for hurried is read backwards

parts.note: raced means hurried

explanation.surface: Someone says they dashed about chasing a little cocktail.
explanation.definitionFit: A drink of brandy, orange liqueur and lemon juice carries this name, the same as a motorcycle's passenger pod.

clue.text: In tears, lady badly corrupted

indicators.note: something done badly is messed up, so the letters of these words are scrambled

explanation.surface: A woman, weeping, has been morally ruined.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone tempted into wrongdoing has been corrupted, misled off the straight path by another's influence.

clue.text: Daughter supports sad hunch about small dog

indicators.note: in a down clue a support sits below, so the daughter's letter goes at the bottom
about means moved around, so the letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A daughter props up someone in a gloomy mood who is worried about a small dog.
explanation.definitionFit: The long-bodied short-legged German breed, nicknamed the sausage dog, is a small hound.

clue.text: File on hospital department is rigorous

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece on another sits above it

parts.note: a file is a line or string of things one after another
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department

explanation.surface: A dossier on a hospital department is strict and thorough.
explanation.definitionFit: Strict, exacting and demanding rules are severe, which fits rigorous.

clue.text: Smallest born escapes from animal by lake

indicators.note: by means beside, so the lake's letter sits next to the rest
what escapes from the animal leaves it, so that letter is removed from the word

parts.note: a beast is an animal

explanation.surface: A newborn creature runs away from its parent beast, near a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'born' is not about the animal's birth here; it is just the letter B, which 'escapes from' removes from the animal word.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of little, meaning tiniest or slightest in amount.

clue.text: Walls of emerald upset my colour scheme

indicators.note: in an across clue upset means the letters are turned round
the walls of a word are its outer letters, its first and last

parts.note: cor and my are both exclamations of surprise

explanation.surface: Someone is dismayed by emerald-green walls in their chosen colour scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'my' is the exclamation, as in 'my, my!', not a possessive; the answer is usually written with an accent.
explanation.definitionFit: The furnishing and paint style of a room is its interior design, which includes its scheme of colours.

clue.text: Mother declines sum awarded by court

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal, especially a horse
ages means grows old, declines with time

explanation.surface: A mother turns down the compensation a court has granted her.
explanation.definitionFit: Money paid in compensation for loss or injury, by order of a judge, is the legal plural term.

clue.text: Former college welcomes politician, old American, in grand manner

indicators.note: welcoming someone means taking them in, so the other pieces go inside

parts.note: a poly, or polytechnic, was a type of British college, most of which became universities in 1992
MP stands for Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: An old polytechnic receives a visiting MP and an elderly American with great ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting self-importantly, with pretentious dignity, is behaving in a grand, puffed-up style.

clue.text: Pale yew, so good now and again as boarding material

indicators.note: now and again means every so often, so take alternate letters starting with the first

explanation.surface: Pale yew wood is good from time to time as a material for boards.
explanation.definitionFit: Thin sheets of wood glued in layers make a cheap panel used for making boards.

clue.text: US police officer alarms suspect outside hotel

indicators.note: the scrambled letters sit outside, around, the hotel letter
suspect means dubious, not straight, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An American lawman alarms a suspect outside a hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: In the United States a federal law officer, or sometimes a sheriff-like officer, holds this title.

clue.text: Keen, say, to vary bets

indicators.note: to vary is to change, so the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone eager is told to spread their wagers.
explanation.walkthrough: In British betting a Yankee is a multiple bet of eleven wagers on four selections; 'say' is part of the fodder, not a signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A bookmaker's multiple wager on four horses gives these combination bets their name.

clue.text: Craft in stone Madonna holding child

indicators.note: the Madonna holds the child, so that word goes inside her name

parts.note: the Madonna is Mary, mother of Jesus
a son is a child

explanation.surface: A stone carving of the Madonna with the infant in her arms.
explanation.definitionFit: Building or carving with cut stone is the stonemason's trade, a skilled craft.

clue.text: Burden on farmers originally facing bad weather

parts.note: re means on, in the sense of concerning

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of the word that follows

parts.note: rain is the bad weather

explanation.surface: Farmers face a burden from a spell of rain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Burden' looks like a load on the farmers but is the old word for a song's chorus.
explanation.definitionFit: A burden is an old term for the repeated chorus of a song, a recurring line or verse.

clue.text: Meeting in favour of you finally having minutes

parts.note: for means in favour of

indicators.note: finally points to the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: At a meeting someone backs you as you finally get the minutes.
explanation.definitionFit: A gathering for public discussion of a subject, as in a debate or assembly.

clue.text: Strange story in article

indicators.note: in places the story inside the article

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
a lie is a story, a falsehood

explanation.surface: An odd tale appears in a newspaper piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'article' looks like a newspaper piece but is the grammatical article AN.
explanation.definitionFit: Foreign and unfamiliar things are strange; the adjective means from elsewhere.

clue.text: Assess fruit across Ukraine's capital

indicators.note: the fruit stretches across, around, the letter that goes inside

parts.note: a gage, or greengage, is a plum-like fruit

indicators.note: a capital letter is the first one, so take the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone sizes up fruit being sold throughout Kyiv.
explanation.definitionFit: To estimate or measure the size of something is to judge or appraise it.

clue.text: Different hybrid of white rose

indicators.note: a hybrid is a cross mixing things, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A rose bred from a white rose comes out unlike its parent.
explanation.walkthrough: The white rose is also the emblem of Yorkshire, adding to the gardening picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done in another way is different; the adverb means in a different manner or else.

clue.text: A little surprised at Edith being given tranquillisers

indicators.note: A little says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone is mildly startled to find Edith on calming medication.
explanation.definitionFit: A patient given calming drugs has been made drowsy and calm by medication.

clue.text: Claiming soldiers last played sad musical pieces

indicators.note: claiming means taking hold of, so the scrambled letters enclose the soldiers
played means the letters of the word are performed in a fresh order

parts.note: men are soldiers, as in officers and men

explanation.surface: Musicians said the soldiers' final number was a sad tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Claiming' and 'played' look like part of a story about soldiers, but one wraps and the other scrambles 'last'.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegies and dirges are mournful songs expressing grief, played as music of sorrow.
